articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Deadline Fantasy Fallout: Colts keep Jonathan Taylor, Chiefs deal for Josh Downs, 49ers land Keenan Allen
articles.summary: It's time to recap some key fantasy-relevant trades.
articles.body:
T he NFL trade deadline is complete and fantasy football is in a whirlwind! Fantasy analyst Joel Smyth breaks down some key deals. And go here for Hayden Winks' breakdown of Kirk Cousins' return to Minnesota .

This trade is not only a win but a lifesaver for Josh Downs' fantasy outlook ( you can read the full trade terms here ). He's the dynasty fantasy winner of the day if he re-signs with the Chiefs, and he can finally be usable in redraft leagues!

The Colts lost Alec Pierce to injury and traded Michael Pittman Jr., yet Downs was still limited to a sub-20% target share. Kansas City has a similar lack of pass-catchers as Indianapolis, but gives Downs more of a chance as one of the most talented receivers in a new offense. He should fit well on a team that has the lowest average depth of target in the NFL.

I'm worried for Rice once Downs is playing full snaps, but researching helped ease concerns a little bit. The negatives: Rice is a volume-dependent WR. He had been recently looking much improved compared to the first few weeks of the season. However, his style is very similar to Downs', running over 50% of routes from the slot, and having over 70% of receiving fantasy points coming on throws under 10 air yards. The big positive here is the schedule, not in terms of fantasy points allowed to WRs, but the game scripts ahead. In a five-game stretch, the Chiefs play the Bills, Rams, Bengals, Patriots and 49ers, all teams that can bump up the passing volume and scoring. Surprisingly, the Chiefs rank third in pass rate over expected, behind only the Packers and Bengals; they have just been consistently in the lead.

The Chiefs' upcoming schedule might be more impactful for Mahomes than Downs, although the deal is a positive. The passing production for Mahomes over the past few years has been modest in fantasy, often relying on his rushing for his ceiling, and I'm not sure this massively changes anything. It's a plus, but maybe a 1-PPG bump compared to having a different wideout in the game.

Jonathan Taylor sticking in Indianapolis

Jonathan Taylor is the lone survivor in Indianapolis. After dealing Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen (more on him below) and Josh Downs, the Colts decided to hold on to Taylor in a failing season without their first-round draft pick available. The share of touches that has dipped down to 63% in the last few weeks should rise back up for Taylor, as there is less reason to save his legs. The only other positives are the schedule should keep some games close, and the receiving, which has often been underrated for Taylor, should be solid overall. However, the negatives win outright, with Taylor's ceiling coming when the touchdowns pile up. Since Week 5, the Colts offense ranks 31st in touchdowns per game with 1.4. He's still startable in fantasy, but the long-term risk is elevated.

Allen has quietly put together a solid fantasy season, outscoring Downs with 10.1 PPR PPG while inside the top 20 WRs in targets. The targets should still be available in San Francisco ( go here for the full trade details ), with no WR having over a 10% target share outside of Mike Evans. The 49ers have been fantasy gold for receivers this decade, often overlooked because of the lack of one sticking long term. Since 2020, they rank first in fantasy points per target and still second in 2026 to the Cincinnati Bengals.

Especially when other wideouts are not available, Allen can continue to be played as a flex option, now more confidently.

articles.title: “These words mean more than you know”: How Travis Kelce repaid former Kansas City Chiefs veteran Dwayne Bowe years after learning what it means to be a great teammate
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has given former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Dwayne Bowe a reason to remember their connection.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has given former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Dwayne Bowe a reason to remember their connection. Bowe helped Kelce understand what it takes to be a good teammate during his early NFL years. More than a decade later, Kelce returned that kindness with a personal gift. In September 2026, he gave Bowe the jersey he wore in the Chiefs’ Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts.Bowe had attended the game, and the gift meant more because of their history together. Kelce later spoke about his former teammate on the New Heights podcast, recalling how Bowe influenced him both inside the locker room and on the field. His words also explained why he was so happy to see the former Chiefs receiver back at the stadium.How Dwayne Bowe became a role model for Travis Kelce in Kansas CityDwayne Bowe arrived in Kansas City as a first-round pick in 2007. By the time the Chiefs drafted Travis Kelce in the third round in 2013, Bowe was already an established player and a respected voice in the offense. Kelce was still finding his place in the NFL, and the veteran gave him an example of how to approach the job.During a September 2026 episode of the New Heights podcast, Travis Kelce remembered Dwayne Bowe as one of the leading figures in the Chiefs locker room during his early seasons.“He was the OG in the locker room and the offense in my early years,” Kelce said.He also credited Bowe with showing younger players how to carry themselves as professionals.“Really showed me what it was to be a great teammate. Somebody who just loved the game of football and loved the atmosphere of being a pro and living out your dreams. He instilled that in everybody in the building, man.”Bowe had earned that respect through his performances as well. He won the Chiefs’ Mack Lee Hill Rookie of the Year award in 2007. His standout season came in 2010, when he caught 72 passes for 1,162 yards and 15 touchdowns. He earned his only Pro Bowl selection that year and made the Second-Team All-Pro roster.Bowe ended his Chiefs career with 532 receptions, 7,155 receiving yards and 44 touchdowns. Those figures remain among the best in franchise history. Travis Kelce’s jersey gift brought their old Chiefs bond back into focusTheir connection made headlines again after Bowe attended Kansas City’s Week 2 game against the Indianapolis Colts in September 2026. On September 28, Bowe shared a social media post revealing that Kelce had given him the jersey from the game.Bowe shared his reaction in the post, writing, “Gr8 B Day 🎁 @tkelce These words mean more than you know. I’ve tried to be the best teammate of our generation.”Kelce also discussed the gesture on the New Heights podcast. He spoke about the respect Bowe earned from people throughout the Chiefs organization.“You can’t find a single person on this Earth that has anything bad to say about Dwayne Bowe, and who he was in the building,” Kelce said.He then shared how he felt about seeing his former teammate return to Chiefs games and ask for his jersey.“To see him coming back to games still and ask me for a jersey, I’m honored, brother.”Bowe moved on from Kansas City in 2015 after signing a two-year contract with the Cleveland Browns. He played seven games for Cleveland and caught five passes. He later signed a one-day contract with the Chiefs to retire with the team that drafted him.Kelce’s gift was a small gesture with a personal history behind it. Bowe had helped him understand the value of being a great teammate when he was still a young player. After years, Kelce used the moment to show that he had never forgotten the lesson.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Drake Maye’s wife Ann Michael shares a festive surprise, revealing the sweet details behind their holiday card
articles.summary: Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael Maye, have found a personal way to celebrate a year filled with major milestones.
articles.body: Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael Maye, have found a personal way to celebrate a year filled with major milestones. The couple’s first holiday card since getting married features a photograph from their anniversary trip to Cabo, offering a glimpse into their life away from the NFL. Ann Michael, 23, shared the card exclusively with PEOPLE on November 10 through her partnership with Minted. Beyond the Christmas greeting, the card carries memories of their travels, their first year of marriage and the quieter moments they have managed to enjoy together.Drake Maye and Ann Michael choose their Cabo anniversary photograph for their holiday cardThe photograph on the front of the card takes the couple back to their first wedding anniversary trip to Cabo during the NFL offseason. Ann Michael wears a brown sundress with blue polka dots, while Drake keeps his look relaxed in a white collared shirt, navy pants and sunglasses. The design, called “Apres Ski” by Wildfield Paper Co., carries a simple “Merry Christmas” message and the Maye family signature.For Ann Michael, the photograph was more than a choice that looked good on a Christmas card. It reminded her of a period when the couple could put their busy schedules aside and enjoy time together.“We chose a photo from our first anniversary trip to Cabo during the offseason. It’s been such an exciting and eventful year for us, and this photo brings back a really happy memory of Drake and me getting to slow down, spend time together, and just soak it all in,” she tells PEOPLE.The couple's relationship has already included several important milestones. Childhood sweethearts, Drake and Ann Michael got engaged in January 2025 and married in June that year. Drake's journey with the New England Patriots also brought plenty of attention, including the team's run to Super Bowl 2026 in February.Amid those developments, Ann Michael said finding time for each other has become particularly valuable.“With everything going on in our lives, those quieter moments together are really special, and I love that we get to share one of them with our friends and family this holiday season,” she says.Ann Michael adds travel memories and plans a Patriots-themed Christmas treeThe Mayes began sending holiday cards only after their wedding, but the tradition has quickly become something Ann Michael looks forward to every year. She sees the cards as a way to preserve memories rather than simply send seasonal greetings.“We started sending holiday cards after we got married, and it’s quickly become a tradition I absolutely love!” Ann Michael shares. “There’s something so special about sending a personal note to friends and family, especially during the holidays.”She also wanted the cards to become a record of their changing lives. “I love the idea of looking back years from now and seeing how our lives have changed through our holiday cards,” she continues, adding, “It’s a sweet way to capture a little snapshot of each year.”There is more to the card than the Cabo photograph. Ann Michael included highlights from the couple's travels on the back, with trips to the Masters and Japan among the memories featured.“One detail you might not notice at first glance is that we included a few highlights from our travels on the back of the card, including trips to the Masters and Japan!” she shares. “We’ve made so many wonderful memories together this year, and I loved being able to share a few more of those moments with our friends and family.”She calls the extra touch “almost like a little year-in-review!”Ann Michael wanted the overall design to feel classic rather than follow a passing trend. Minted's independent artist designs and concierge service helped her find a style that matched the photograph and the couple's taste. She also has plans to bring some football spirit into their Christmas celebrations, even though the holiday card itself does not feature the Patriots.“I am planning a Patriots-themed red and blue Christmas tree this holiday season!” she shares.Her hope is that the card makes friends and family smile. After a year of marriage, travel and major football moments, the Mayes have chosen to preserve something less public: the memories they made together.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: All about Patrick Mahomes' three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden, as he and Brittany prepare to welcome baby No. 4
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, are preparing to welcome their fourth child, adding another member to a family that has grown alongside
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, are preparing to welcome their fourth child, adding another member to a family that has grown alongside the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback's remarkable NFL career. The couple already share three children: Sterling Skye, Patrick “Bronze” Lavon Mahomes III and Golden Raye. From Sterling's first appearance on the football field to Bronze and Golden joining their parents at major family celebrations, each child has had a special place in their lives. Their growing family also reflects Patrick's approach to fatherhood, which has always centered on letting his children find their own interests.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are preparing to welcome their fourth childThe Mahomes family is getting ready for another major change. Patrick and Brittany have already experienced the demands and happiness of raising three young children, and baby No. 4 will make their household even bigger.The couple's journey into parenthood began in 2021, shortly after Patrick proposed to Brittany at the Kansas City Chiefs' Super Bowl ring ceremony on September 1, 2020. Later that month, they announced that they were expecting their first child.Brittany shared the pregnancy news with a photograph of the couple holding a sonogram, writing, “Just taking a small detour to the wedding😬❤️.”They married on March 12, 2022, in a ceremony that included their daughter Sterling as the flower girl. Patrick had previously told PEOPLE that he hoped his daughter would be part of the wedding. Brittany later confirmed that Sterling had indeed taken on the role, making the occasion even more special for the family.Sterling Skye Mahomes was their first childSterling Skye Mahomes was born on February 20, 2021, in Kansas City, Missouri. Patrick and Brittany announced her arrival with a photograph of their newborn holding her father's finger. Their announcement also revealed her birth details: 6 pounds and 11 ounces.The couple initially decided against sharing Sterling's face publicly. Brittany explained that they wanted to wait until they felt comfortable doing so. Sterling eventually made her Instagram debut in June 2021, four months after her birth.She soon became a familiar face among Chiefs fans. Sterling appeared alongside her father in an Oakley commercial, giving Patrick another reason to celebrate his daughter's growing personality.“We got a special day. We got Ster-Ster’s first commercial,” Patrick said at the time. “She’s going to be the real star of the family.”Sterling has also developed a noticeable connection with her father's football career. During the 2022 season, she and Brittany wore matching Chiefs-inspired outfits, including red pants and black shirts with the Mahomes name.Her game-day wardrobe became even more personal in 2024. Sterling wore a custom denim outfit featuring patches referencing Patrick, including his jersey number and the word “daddy.”Brittany spoke about her daughter's excitement around game days in January 2024. “She truly enjoys going down to the field and getting to see him before the game,” she told PEOPLE. “I think it’s a very special moment wherever I get to bring them to the game and they get to watch their dad play football.”Patrick “Bronze” Mahomes III joined the family in 2022The Mahomes family welcomed its first son on November 28, 2022. Patrick and Brittany announced his arrival through Instagram, introducing him as Patrick “Bronze” Lavon Mahomes III.The announcement featured a photograph of the newborn's feet resting on a fleece blanket bearing the Mahomes name. A custom diamond chain with Bronze's name was also placed beside him.His arrival brought a new dynamic to the household. Brittany had already experienced motherhood with Sterling, but managing two young children presented its own challenges.In December 2022, she offered a glimpse of those early parenting days on X, writing, “Today is my first day of chaos since having 2 kids,” before adding, “Both screaming, both not wanting to nap.”Bronze also became part of the family's Super Bowl traditions at an early age. He accompanied Brittany and Sterling to the 2023 Super Bowl in Arizona and the 2024 championship game in Las Vegas.Patrick even celebrated his son's second birthday through a footwear collaboration. Ahead of the occasion in November 2024, the quarterback unveiled the Mahomes 2 Impact FLX Bronze training shoes with Adidas.“Celebrating Bronze’s birthday with his own colorway,” Patrick wrote on Instagram.Golden Raye Mahomes completed their family of fivePatrick and Brittany welcomed their third child, Golden Raye Mahomes, on January 12, 2025. The couple announced her arrival through a joint Instagram post featuring a black-and-white photograph of their daughter's tiny feet held by her parents.“•Golden Raye Mahomes•1/12/25🎀✨,” the announcement read.They had revealed the pregnancy in July 2024 with a family video documenting a photoshoot. “Round three, here we come,” they wrote alongside the announcement. The couple later confirmed that they were expecting another girl.Golden's name also continued the family's distinctive naming tradition. Sterling, Bronze and Golden all draw inspiration from precious metals, giving the three siblings a shared connection through their names.Her first birthday in January 2026 brought another family celebration. Brittany shared footage from a flower-themed party featuring a bouncy castle and a ball pit.“Celebrated our Golden girl with the best crew,” she wrote.Patrick Mahomes wants his children to choose their own pathWhile football is central to Patrick's professional life, he has made it clear that he does not intend to push his children towards the same career.During an October 2022 appearance on Football in America, the quarterback discussed how he planned to approach his children's potential sporting interests.“I'm going to teach my son, my daughter all the fundamentals and whatever they want to learn,” the three-time Super Bowl MVP explained. “But at the same time ... I want to let it be about them ... That's what my dad did growing up, that's what my parents did. They didn't pressure me to do anything. I think that's why I'm in the position I am today.”That approach offers a glimpse into how Patrick views his responsibilities away from the NFL. He wants his children to have the freedom to explore their interests rather than inherit expectations because of their father's achievements.With Sterling, Bronze and Golden already part of the family, the arrival of their fourth child will bring another chapter to the Mahomes household. Patrick may be one of football's biggest stars, but his own words suggest that he wants his children to build identities that have little to do with his reputation on the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Could Drew Brees really return to the NFL? Former Saints QB reveals why throwing to Justin Jefferson tempts him
articles.summary: Drew Brees has not completely given up on the idea of playing in the NFL again.
articles.body: Drew Brees has not completely given up on the idea of playing in the NFL again. The former New Orleans Saints quarterback recently admitted that throwing to Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson would make a return tempting. His comments came as Minnesota dealt with questions at quarterback despite its strong 6-2 start to the 2026 season.The conversation picked up after Troy Aikman suggested that Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell would welcome Brees back. However, Brees' latest remarks offer a more personal reason behind the idea. He enjoys watching Jefferson and believes playing alongside the star receiver would be fun.Drew Brees explains how Troy Aikman brought the Vikings comeback idea into the spotlightThe idea first came up during a casual conversation between Brees and his broadcasting colleagues. While watching the Vikings play, the former quarterback was messaging Tony Gonzalez, who also works with Fox. Brees joked that he might leave the broadcast booth and join Minnesota.Speaking to Adam Kaufman on USA Today Sports, Brees explained how the conversation reached Aikman.“I’m broadcasting the Packers-Vikings game this coming weekend, and I said, ‘I may come out of the booth and play quarterback for the Vikings,’” Brees recalled.He also explained why the thought appealed to him. Minnesota has a talented defense, while Jefferson remains one of the receivers he enjoys watching most.Brees added that Jefferson has long been one of his favourite players. He even revealed that his children follow the Vikings receiver and have him on their fantasy football team. That gives his interest in throwing to Jefferson a personal touch beyond the football conversation.Aikman then took the joke to a much bigger audience. During ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast on November 9, while the Vikings faced the Buffalo Bills, he told Joe Buck that Brees was considering retirement.“I told him if he does, Kevin O’Connell will sign him tomorrow,” Aikman said during the broadcast.Buck agreed with the suggestion, but the exchange also highlighted Minnesota's growing quarterback concerns.Vikings' quarterback struggles make Drew Brees' Jefferson comments more interestingMinnesota entered its November 9 matchup with Buffalo at 6-2, but its offense struggled badly in the 23-6 defeat. Carson Wentz, who started in place of injured Kyler Murray, completed just eight of 25 passes for 81 yards and threw two interceptions. Head coach Kevin O'Connell eventually turned to backup Max Brosmer late in the game.The performance put further attention on the Vikings' quarterback situation. Their defense has given the team a strong foundation, but the offense needs more consistent production. Jefferson is among the players who could benefit from a reliable quarterback.Brees, however, has already explained why an NFL comeback would be difficult. The 47-year-old retired after the 2020 season following a remarkable career with the San Diego Chargers and New Orleans Saints. He has not played a regular-season game since.There was also a genuine opportunity to return earlier in 2026. After Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix suffered an injury during the playoffs in January, Brees considered stepping in for the AFC Championship Game. The Broncos ultimately went with Jarrett Stidham.During his September appearance on the Let's Go podcast with Jim Gray, Brees explained that his throwing wrist and shoulder prevented him from making the comeback happen.“My mind, my body, everything else feels great, but my right wrist, right shoulder wouldn’t allow it to happen,” Brees said.He admitted that he had seriously considered the Broncos opportunity, but his physical condition stopped him.That makes his latest Vikings comments more of a fun possibility than an indication of an actual return. Brees clearly likes the idea of throwing to Jefferson, but his previous injury concerns remain a major obstacle. For Minnesota, finding a dependable quarterback remains a much more realistic priority than expecting the former Saints star to trade his headset for a helmet.Brees' career numbers explain why Aikman's suggestion caught attention. He finished his NFL career with 80,358 passing yards and 571 touchdown passes, along with a Super Bowl title with the Saints. Still, his throwing injuries make another comeback extremely unlikely.As of now, the Vikings will have to find answers without him. Brees may enjoy the thought of throwing to Jefferson, but Minnesota needs a quarterback who can actually get the ball to its star receiver.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How the Chiefs' Josh Downs move could reshape Tyreek Hill's comeback prospects and Patrick Mahomes' receiving options
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs landed fourth-year slot receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts at the trade deadline.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs landed fourth-year slot receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts at the trade deadline. The price was a 2027 fourth-round pick and a fifth-rounder, with a 2027 seventh coming back. It hands Patrick Mahomes another target right now. It also complicates the talk of a Tyreek Hill reunion, which had been loud for weeks. Hill, a five-time All-Pro, is 32, not yet medically cleared and facing a possible suspension. With Downs in the building, Kansas City no longer needs a quick fix, and Hill was never going to be one.How the Downs trade changes the Tyreek Hill and Patrick Mahomes pictureDowns will line up next to Rashee Rice, the team’s top receiver, and Travis Kelce. For Mahomes, that means a dependable option underneath, which is where Downs works best. He is quick and shifty, but he is not a deep threat. Hill is a different animal. He is an ultra-fast All-Pro who also runs a full route tree, so on paper the two barely overlap.Mahomes gets something else from this. Rice and Kelce give him proven targets, and Downs adds a slot option who can win quickly on short throws. That is a floor-raising move. Hill would be a ceiling-raising one, and ceilings only count if the team is still playing in January.Kansas City still has a gap to fill. Worthy is expected to be out, so the Chiefs must still start one of Royals or Allen. Downs is a short-term answer to that. Hill is not available yet. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Hill’s return is delayed because he is not medically cleared, a hurdle expected to fall in the next “few weeks”.Why Tyreek Hill looks like a playoff-only optionThen there is the league office. Hill was found liable for two counts of battery in October, tied to incidents in 2024 and 2025 involving his ex-wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill. A personal conduct policy case is ongoing.The minimum suspension for domestic violence is six weeks if he is found in violation, and given the allegations it could run longer. Add the weeks he still needs for medical clearance and the math gets ugly fast. The regular season could be mostly gone before Hill ever suits up. That makes him a playoffs-or-bust idea, unless the league again decides not to suspend him, as it once did.Say he clears both hurdles. Rice, Worthy and Downs form the starting group, with Royals and Allen behind them. Hill would add something none of them offers, but he would arrive after a serious, long-term injury and play a handful of games. Is that worth the negative publicity and the hit to the franchise’s name?If the Chiefs pass, Mahomes still has a fuller receiver room than he did a week ago. They paid real picks for Downs. For Hill they have paid nothing, and a no would not surprise anyone.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL trade deadline winners and losers: Vikings go full dadcore with Kirk Cousins in Super Bowl quest
articles.summary: Teams with championship aspirations tooled up at the deadline. Most, but not all of them, have improved their chances
articles.body:
The Vikings get the QB they desperately need

After what happened on Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings had to do this. In a dispiriting loss to the Buffalo Bills, the Vikings saw their tremendous defense go to waste, as Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 8.9. It was one of the worst quarterback performances in recent history , and it continued a run of recent QB futility for the Vikings, from JJ McCarthy to Kyler Murray to Wentz. Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is out-scheming every other coach in the league right now with his laboratory of blitzes and coverages. But it's starting to matter less and less, because opposing offenses know that you can wait that defense out when there's no juice on the other side of the ball. The Vikings rank first in scoring defense (116 points allowed), but they're 27th in points scored (146).

This is not sustainable, which is why Minnesota welcomed ur-suburban dad Kirk Cousins back to the team he led from 2018-2023 by sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders . The 38-year-old is in his 15th NFL season, and he's not quite the player he used to be, but he's a massive improvement over everyone else in the Vikings building at his position. This season, Cousins has completed 202 of 315 passes for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, eight interceptions, and a passer rating of 97.1. The rest of the Vikings QBs this season have combined for 137 of 225 passes for 1,286 yards, eight touchdowns, five interceptions, and a passer rating of 82.0.

Cousins enters an NFC North that may be the most brutally competitive division in NFL history , but if he plays like he has this season so far, the Vikings have more than a puncher's chance.

Do the Vikings like that ? We suspect that they do. And in addition to his play on the field, he should bring a maturity and calm to the quarterback position in Minnesota, something that McCarthy and Murray's critics have said they have lacked at points during their careers.

As for the Raiders, they essentially pick up a free third-rounder after signing Cousins to a one-year, $11.3m fully guaranteed contract, and selecting Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza with the first overall pick in the 2026 draft. The plan all along was for Cousins to start until Mendoza was ready for the rigors of the NFL . We're about to see if he is.

The Bears go all-in (and win) with the Jeffery Simmons trade

It usually takes a minute for a traded player, no matter how good he may be, to make a considerable difference with his new team. That player has to deal with a new city, teammates and schemes– it's not an easy adjustment. But when the Chicago Bears traded 2027 and 2028 first-round draft picks and a 2027 fourth-rounder to the Tennessee Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick … well, it cost a lot, but it made Chicago's defense better – immediately. Per SumerSports, the Bears have gone from 6.39 to 4.45 yards per play allowed with Simmons on the field, and he's made other Chicago defenders better, from edge rusher (and former Mississippi State teammate) Montez Sweat to linebacker Devin Bush.

In Chicago's 27-24 Sunday night win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, it was that defense which took over, as the usually potent Bears offense had its issues against the Bucs' top-tier defense. Caleb Williams threw four interceptions, and Chicago won a game in which they committed five or more turnovers for the first time since they did so twice in the 2006 season – including a 24-23 win over the Arizona Cardinals that led to the greatest postgame press conference ever, courtesy of Cardinals head coach Dennis Green .

With the offense playing at its usual pace and the defense at an entirely new level, the Simmons trade is a prime example of what a big-time trade should do – turn a good team into a great one.

Seattle's Quenton Nelson trade may hit its own unfortunate deadline

The Seattle Seahawks needed to revive a run game that has been below average since the team let last season's Super Bowl MVP, Kenneth Walker III, walk to the Kansas City Chiefs. They believed they can solve their rushing problem by sending a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick to the Indianapolis Colts for offensive guard Quenton Nelson, the eight-time Pro Bowler who will eventually find his way to the Hall of Fame.

Nelson still has plenty to offer at the age of 30. But these deals don't always work out the way teams hope. Seattle's first game with Nelson was a 34-17 loss to the Bears, who came into Lumen Field with Simmons in tow, and wrecked any offensive plans the Seahawks made. Nelson is a left guard, which meant that the Seahawks moved 2025 first-round pick Grey Zabel to the right side, where he hadn't played since 2023, when he was at North Dakota State.

Moving from one side to the other is never as easy for offensive linemen as people may think, and the Bears wisely lined Simmons up more on Zabel's side than Nelson's – 88% to 12%, per Pro Football Focus. This allowed Simmons and his energized cohorts to pressure Sam Darnold ceaselessly, and the quarterback is now out with a quadriceps injury and a cracked rib.

Backup Drew Lock started Seattle's win over the Arizona Cardinals last week, and Zabel moved back to the left side, because Nelson is now recovering from a knee procedure, and is week-to-week.

Why is this a problem? Because Nelson won't have time to acclimate to his new line, and Zabel won't have time to acclimate to his new right side. Plus, Nelson is in the final year of the four-year, $80m contract extension he signed in 2022. If Nelson misses significant time, and the 5-4 Seahawks can't find their way into the playoffs, whatever positive effects Nelson's acquisition might have provided will be meaningless in the long term.

It has become more than apparent that the Jacksonville Jaguars are all-in this season. Which makes sense. The 6-2 Jags lead the NFL in point differential (+108) and turnover differential (+9), and after their 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens last Thursday, they rank first overall in DVOA for the first time in the history of the franchise – which goes back to 1996.

Which is why general manager James Gladstone made the call to trade a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons for safety Jessie Bates III. Jacksonville have been assembling their safety rotation with spit and baling wire of late and have a lot of injuries to deal with, and Bates is one of the NFL's better and more versatile players at his position(s) . He's an expert defender everywhere from the box to the slot to the deep third.

The Jags also traded a sixth-round pick for New Orleans Saints interior defensive lineman Davon Godchaux. This also works because the 6ft 3in, 330lbs Godchaux is a good rotational run defender, and the Jags recently lost DaVon Hamilton, the heartbeat of their run defense, to a season-ending injury.

But as it turns out, those moves were just the opening acts. Gladstone then made a massive deal with the Philadelphia Eagles, trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for defensive lineman Jordan Davis.

And this is where Gladstone and the Jaguars may be a bit over their skis.

Selected with the 13th overall pick in the 2022 draft out of Georgia, Davis was a highly-regarded interior disruptor based on his college work, but that promise never quite developed in the ways in which the Eagles hoped. The 6ft 6in, 336lbs Davis has all the athleticism and power you'd want, but the results have been middling to disappointing. Davis has never amassed more than five sacks and 28 pressures in a season. Those totals both came in 2025, after which the Eagles signed him to a three-year, $78m contract extension.

Davis has become an above-average run defender, but when you're giving up future first- and second-round picks for a player, you want more than that, right? Especially when you consider what the Bears paid for Simmons, and what they've gotten out of that deal already. Simmons is a truly transformative player; Davis at his level best is more of a well-turned cog in a machine.

Maybe Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile can extract more from Davis than his Eagles counterpart, Vic Fangio, ever did. But given Fangio's overall expertise (more than half the defenses in the NFL apply at least some of Fangio's principles), it's a steep bet at that price.

– The San Francisco 49ers poked around the Colts' fire sale and plucked out DeForest Buckner for a fourth-round pick, and receiver Keenan Allen for a sixth-round pick. These weren't what you'd call franchise-transforming moves, but Kyle Shanahan's offense can really use some receiver help with all the injuries they've seen this season, and Buckner can add to a defensive line that has been similarly beat up. As always, it is impossible to write more than two sentences about the 49ers without mentioning injuries, and that dastardly substation curse .

– Speaking of Colts receivers, the Chiefs acquired Josh Downs and a seventh-round draft pick for fourth-round and fifth-round picks. Patrick Mahomes's team have been in receiver purgatory for a long time, and while Downs won't blow you away with his production (33 catches on 57 targets this season for 354 yards and a touchdown), he can be one of those sneaky-good guys with an understanding of the nuances of his position. The Chiefs' leading non-Travis Kelce receiver this season is Xavier Worthy, who has 278 receiving yards and a touchdown. Maybe Downs fills in the gaps. He certainly seems happy about his new home .

– The Bills made one of the day's smartest moves when they sent a second-round pick to the Titans for safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick. Buffalo's safety situation has been less than optimal in 2026 – between CJ Gardner-Johnson (who was released after poor play and a spitting suspension ), Cole Bishop, and Damar Hamlin, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has had issues. Hooker comes in with far more of a pedigree – this season, he's tied with Xavier McKinney of the Green Bay Packers for the NFL's most interceptions with five, and the veteran will help to knit the entire pass defense together .

articles.title: Commanders' offensive lineman reveals mental health struggles
articles.summary: It's been a tough year for Nick Allegretti. He opened up on how tough it's been.
articles.body:
It hasn't been a fun few months for Washington Commanders offensive lineman Nick Allegretti. The year started off on a good note when Allegretti signed a new two-year deal in March and was expected to become Washington's starting center in 2026 after the Commanders surprisingly released Tyler Biadasz.

It was a curious move to cut Biadasz. It's not that he was great last season, but many believed the Commanders only cut him to sign former Ravens center Tyler Linderbaum in free agency. That plan backfired when the Raiders blew Linderbaum out of the water with a massive offer. Instead of looking elsewhere for an experienced center, Washington turned to Allegretti, who had mostly played guard throughout his NFL career.

Allegretti was excited for the opportunity. He had played some center in college at Illinois and had always felt it was the position where he was most comfortable. Every chance they got, Washington general manager Adam Peters and head coach Dan Quinn praised Allegretti. Fans were concerned, especially considering the Commanders were going with a new offense, and quarterback Jayden Daniels would be under center more. But Peters and Quinn were insistent that Allegretti would ease those concerns.

Then, at the beginning of training camp, Allegretti suffered a calf injury. Washington's plan backfired. Not only was there a question of whether Allegretti could be a quality starting center, but what was Peters' backup plan if Allegretti was either injured or ineffective?

The answers were journeyman Julian Good-Jones and rookie sixth-round pick Matt Gulbin. The results weren't pretty. Fans and media took turns saying, "I told you so."

The Commanders' response: "Relax, we'll be fine when Nick is back."

Allegretti was back for Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles. He struggled. Those struggles continued in Week 2. In Week 3, after the Commanders signed veteran center/guard Lucas Patrick, they moved Allegretti to right guard to replace Sam Cosmi, who was out with a concussion. Patrick took over at center.

After that week, Quinn confirmed Patrick was now the starting center. Allegretti was back on the bench. Then, last week, when Patrick was injured, Washington turned to Gulbin—not Allegretti. It didn't make sense. After the game, Quinn said it was because Allegretti had been taking practice reps at guard.

On Tuesday, Quinn confirmed Patrick was in concussion protocol, and Allegretti would start Thursday's game against the New York Giants.

"Yes, Nick will be starting at center," Quinn said. "He was working mostly at guard some, the last couple [weeks], been banged up some, and so with the full week of prep, Nick will be back at center."

Allegretti also spoke to reporters in the locker room on Tuesday and acknowledged how difficult the last couple of months have been for him, between injuries and being in and out of the lineup.

"I think pretty well," Allegretti responded when asked how he's mentally handled all the changes and uncertainty. "I've worked with some mental health coaches on that, just cause it's a tough process. You know, handling some injuries and being in and out of the lineup. For a long time in my career, I kind of just kept all of that to myself. Working through that these last couple of years has helped me a ton. I think it's helped me day to day. Just to truly enjoy being here, being in the locker room, regardless of what my role is. Taking that role seriously, and now I have another opportunity to be in the role I obviously truly want, and I'm excited for it."

Why is Allegretti so open about having a mental health coach?

"Just because of how much it helped me," Allegretti said. "It's one of those things that you — as men, we're just lulled into this, 'Don't talk about it. Handle your things yourself.' I tried for a long time, and I got to a point where it was too much for me. And I'll say probably one of the reasons that I handle the day-to-day here well when I'm not playing is just all the people that were here for me. Helped me get the help that I needed. Not just in the locker room, but some coaching and staff members really went out of their way to make sure I was right. It's a process; I'm still working weekly with that."

This was powerful stuff from Allegretti. He didn't mention it, but there is also the cold, cruel, soulless world of social media. Where "fans" insult players they've never met over a game. They say things they'd never say to that player. Over a game. When Allegretti missed a block, those same "fans" would make it personal. Allegretti may or may not have seen or read those things. Hopefully, he didn't.

I've stated more than once that Washington set Allegretti up for failure, even if it wasn't on purpose. I don't think Peters or Quinn were purposely putting outrageous expectations on Allegretti. They believed in him. And even if they had concerns, they couldn't acknowledge those concerns.

And an injury in training camp didn't help. He missed valuable reps and was still working his way back when he was sidelined. But kudos to everyone in the Commanders' organization for looking after Allegretti. In the end, those are the things that matter most.

Allegretti is brave. There aren't many athletes who would stand up there and talk so freely about mental health. He did. And he likely made some new fans. It's sometimes easy to forget that these men and women we see on TV playing college or pro sports are human beings, too. They battle with mental health issues, whether it's personal or related to their chosen sport. They're unfairly ridiculed on social media.

Allegretti doesn't need to prove anything to anyone. He's an eight-year NFL pro. He's a three-time Super Bowl champion who has appeared in 115 career games with 37 starts. Not bad for a former seventh-round pick.

Here's hoping Allegretti crushes it on Thursday night.

articles.title: 49ers face Mike Evans injury setback as Super Bowl hopes hinge on his return
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers have been handed another concerning Mike Evans injury update as doubts grow over the wide receiver’s availability for their upcoming...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have been handed another concerning Mike Evans injury update as doubts grow over the wide receiver's availability for their upcoming clash with the Dallas Cowboys.

Evans has missed the last two games with Achilles tendinitis and the 49ers do not expect him to practise when they begin their preparations for the Cowboys. His absence could stretch further if the injury does not improve.

San Francisco recently added veteran receiver Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. However, the move does not necessarily solve the bigger problem facing Kyle Shanahan's offence.

Mike Evans' fitness could determine the San Francisco 49ers' Super Bowl chances

Evans' importance to the 49ers became clear during his first six appearances after joining the team in the off-season.

The veteran caught 27 of his 39 targets for 420 yards and three touchdowns, quickly developing a connection with quarterback Brock Purdy. He also provided the kind of outside receiving threat that San Francisco has struggled to replace during his absence.

NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco believes the 49ers' championship ambitions could depend on getting Evans back to full fitness.

Speaking about the situation, Maiocco said: "If the missing piece is missing, the 49ers will be missing out on a championship. The margin for error is thin in the NFL. It's such a long season and a lot of things have to go right, including luck, to be the last team standing."

He also highlighted the impact Evans made before his injury, adding: "He was a first-down machine, as he caught 27 passes for 420 yards and three touchdowns."

Maiocco believes the 49ers need to be careful with the receiver's recovery rather than rushing him back before he is ready.

Evans joined San Francisco for his 13th NFL season after signing a below-market contract because he believed the team had a genuine chance of winning the Super Bowl.

The 49ers remain in a strong position at 7-1 and top of the NFC West. However, their lack of a recognised No. 1 outside receiver without Evans remains a concern.

Allen's arrival gives Purdy another experienced option, but Evans offers a different dimension to the offence. San Francisco will be hoping his recovery progresses quickly as the games become increasingly important.
